MedicalEntity: Any thing related to health and medicine. Also called medical concept, health entity.
MedicalIntangible: An abstract medical concept that is not a physical object. Also called medical abstraction.
AnatomicalStructure: Any part of the body: an organ, tissue, or cell. Also called body part, anatomical part. Examples: heart, femur, skin.
AnatomicalSystem: A group of body structures working together for a function. Also called organ system, body system. Examples: circulatory system, nervous system.
BrainStructure: A part of the brain or nervous coordinating tissue. Also called brain region, neural structure. Examples: hippocampus, cerebellum.
Bone: Rigid connective tissue forming the skeleton. Also called osseous tissue. Examples: femur, skull.
Joint: The point where two or more bones meet. Also called articulation. Examples: knee, elbow.
Ligament: Tough fibrous tissue connecting bones at joints. Also called connective band.
Nerve: A bundle of fibres carrying nerve impulses. Also called nerve fibre. Examples: sciatic nerve, optic nerve.
Vessel: A hollow tube carrying blood through the body. Also called blood vessel. Examples: artery, vein.
Artery: A blood vessel carrying blood away from the heart. Also called arterial vessel. Examples: aorta.
Vein: A blood vessel carrying blood toward the heart. Also called venous vessel.
LymphaticVessel: A vessel carrying lymph fluid toward the heart. Also called lymph vessel.
SuperficialAnatomy: Anatomical features visible or palpable on the body surface. Also called surface anatomy.
Substance: Matter of defined composition with discrete existence, biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, matter.
MedicalCondition: Any condition affecting normal body or mental functioning. Also called disease, disorder, illness, ailment, syndrome. Examples: diabetes, asthma.
InfectiousDisease: A disease caused by pathogenic microbes such as viruses or bacteria. Also called contagious disease, communicable disease. Examples: influenza, tuberculosis.
MedicalConditionStage: A defined stage in the progression of a medical condition. Also called disease stage. Examples: Stage IIIa.
MedicalCause: The agent responsible for a medical condition, symptom, or sign. Also called cause, aetiology, causative agent.
MedicalSignOrSymptom: Any feature or manifestation associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical feature, manifestation.
MedicalSign: An objective manifestation of a condition found by examination or tests. Also called clinical sign. Examples: fever, swelling.
MedicalSymptom: A subjective complaint reported by a patient. Also called complaint. Examples: pain, fatigue, nausea.
VitalSign: A measure of a basic physiological function. Also called vital. Examples: heart rate, blood pressure, temperature.
MedicalRiskFactor: Anything increasing the likelihood of a disease or complication. Also called risk factor. Examples: smoking, obesity.
MedicalProcedure: A process of care for diagnosis, treatment, prevention, or palliation. Also called procedure, intervention, operation.
DiagnosticProcedure: A medical procedure performed to diagnose a condition. Also called diagnostic test, work-up.
TherapeuticProcedure: A medical procedure performed to treat a condition. Also called treatment, therapy.
SurgicalProcedure: A medical procedure involving incision with instruments. Also called surgery, operation.
PalliativeProcedure: A procedure to relieve symptoms rather than cure. Also called palliative care.
MedicalTherapy: A medical intervention to prevent, treat, or cure conditions. Also called therapy, treatment.
OccupationalTherapy: Therapy using purposeful activity to help people overcome physical or social problems. Also called OT.
PhysicalTherapy: Rehabilitation using physical methods to improve a condition. Also called physiotherapy, physio.
RadiationTherapy: Treatment using radiation. Also called radiotherapy.
PsychologicalTreatment: Treatment of mental health through counselling and dialogue. Also called psychotherapy, talk therapy, counselling.
LifestyleModification: Care involving diet, exercise, and lifestyle changes to improve health. Also called lifestyle change.
MedicalTest: Any medical test, usually for diagnosis. Also called diagnostic test, examination, screening.
BloodTest: A medical test performed on a blood sample. Also called blood work, blood panel.
ImagingTest: A diagnostic test using medical imaging. Also called scan, imaging. Examples: X-ray, MRI, CT scan.
PathologyTest: A laboratory test examining a tissue sample. Also called pathology, lab test, biopsy analysis.
MedicalTestPanel: A set of tests commonly ordered together. Also called test panel, lab panel.
MedicalDevice: An object used to diagnose or treat patients. Also called medical instrument, apparatus. Examples: pacemaker, stethoscope.
MedicalStudy: A research study on human health or medicine. Also called clinical study, medical research.
MedicalTrial: A controlled study comparing safety and efficacy of treatments. Also called clinical trial, randomized trial.
MedicalObservationalStudy: A study inferring treatment effects by observing subjects over time. Also called observational study, cohort study.
MedicalGuideline: An official recommendation on diagnosing or treating a condition. Also called clinical guideline, practice guideline.
MedicalGuidelineRecommendation: A guideline recommendation supported by sound evidence. Also called clinical recommendation.
MedicalGuidelineContraindication: A guideline statement that a process is harmful, with sound supporting data. Also called contraindication guideline.
MedicalRiskEstimator: A tool or rule set for estimating disease or complication risk. Also called risk tool, risk model.
MedicalRiskCalculator: An online calculator for estimating prognosis. Also called risk calculator.
MedicalRiskScore: A score summing risk factors to indicate prognosis. Also called risk score. Examples: CHADS score.
MedicalIndication: A condition or factor indicating use of a therapy. Also called indication.
ApprovedIndication: An indication formally approved by a regulator. Also called approved use.
PreventionIndication: An indication for preventing a condition. Also called preventive indication.
TreatmentIndication: An indication for treating a condition. Also called therapeutic indication.
MedicalContraindication: A reason to withhold a therapy. Also called contraindication.
DrugClass: A category of drugs sharing action or effect. Also called drug category. Examples: statins, antibiotics.
DrugCost: The cost per unit of a medical drug. Also called drug price, medication cost.
DrugLegalStatus: The legal availability status of a drug. Also called drug status.
DrugStrength: The strength a drug is available in for a country. Also called dosage strength.
DoseSchedule: A dosing schedule for a drug or supplement. Also called dosing regimen, dosage schedule.
MaximumDoseSchedule: The maximum safe dosing schedule for a drug. Also called maximum dose.
RecommendedDoseSchedule: The recommended dosing schedule for a drug. Also called recommended dose.
ReportedDoseSchedule: A patient-reported or observed dosing schedule. Also called reported dose.
DDxElement: An alternative related condition considered in differential diagnosis. Also called differential, DDx item.
